quickAnswer: Cleaning a 30,000 sq ft business campus with 8 restrooms costs $1,470 to $2,940 per visit on a 5x/week weekday schedule ($31,825 to $63,651 per month) or $1,545 to $3,090 per visit on a 3x/week schedule ($20,085 to $40,170 per month). Using the 25,000+ sq ft enterprise bracket ($0.05 to $0.10 per sq ft) plus $120 to $240 per visit for eight restrooms, a campus requires 8.70 to 12.71 ISSA labor hours per visit.

blocks.text: At **30,000 square feet**, a multi-suite corporate campus operates like a mini commercial building rather than an oversized tenant suite. With **8 restrooms** distributed across wings or floors, multiple breakrooms, training auditoriums, and heavy lobby glass, labor planning shifts to **8.70 to 12.71 ISSA technician hours per visit**—meaning a full three- or four-person evening crew works simultaneously under a site lead.

Our [Office Cleaning Cost Guides](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/) model places 30,000 sq ft solidly inside the **$0.05 to $0.10 per sq ft** enterprise tier. Still, the gap between a bare-bones **$31,825/month** weekday contract and a turnkey **$82,988/month** full-service proposal comes down to three controllable levers: **restroom fixture density**, **flooring surface multipliers**, and **paper consumables ownership**.
30,000 Sq Ft Campus Pricing by Cleaning Frequency (8 Restrooms)

The benchmark matrix below reflects **30,000 cleanable sq ft** of commercial carpet (**1.00x multiplier**) and **8 restrooms** (**$120 to $240 per visit** at **$15 to $30 per restroom**) at the **1.00x US national average**. At **5x/week** (**21.65 visits/month** at **0.90x**), per-visit cost settles at **$1,470 to $2,940** (**$381,906 to $763,812 per year**). At **3x/week** (**13.00 visits/month** at **0.95x**), per-visit cost runs **$1,545 to $3,090** (**$241,020 to $482,040 per year**).

blocks.text: Restrooms, Flooring Multipliers, and Turnkey Add-On Economics

On a 30,000 sq ft campus, **8 restrooms** consume **1.20 to 2.00 labor hours every night** (**0.15 to 0.25 hrs per restroom**) plus **$120 to $240 per visit** in core sanitation pricing. Meanwhile, hard-floor choices shift monthly spend sharply on a 5x/week contract: **polished concrete (0.95x)** trims the monthly range to **$30,364–$60,728**, whereas **VCT/LVT vinyl (1.04x)** lifts it to **$32,995–$65,989**, **mixed floors (1.05x)** reach **$33,287–$66,574**, and **ceramic tile and grout (1.12x)** push monthly cost to **$35,333–$70,666**.

The biggest single jump comes from **vendor-supplied paper and soap consumables** (**$0.012 to $0.025/sq ft/visit**), which adds **$360 to $750 per visit**—or **$7,795 to $16,237 per month** on a 5x/week schedule. Adding **quarterly deep floor care** (**$0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month**) contributes another **$900 to $1,800 per month**, while **breakroom sanitation** (**+$12–$25/visit**) and **interior glass** (**+$15–$35/visit**) add modest fixed fees.

blocks.title: Audit 8-Restroom Fixture Counts Before Signing a Flat Per-Restroom Rate
blocks.text: Our $15–$30 per-restroom benchmark spans single-user executive baths up to 4-to-6-fixture multi-stall restrooms. On a 30,000 sq ft campus where several restrooms hold 6+ toilets, urinals, and sinks, expect bids near $25–$30 per restroom ($200–$240/visit) rather than $15—and inspect chrome, partitions, and grout monthly.
Regional Metro Costs, Shift Handoffs, and Specialty Add-On Rates

Labor-market geography alters 30,000 sq ft quotes substantially. In **Atlanta, GA (1.01x)**, a 5x/week carpeted campus mirrors the national table at roughly **$1,485 to $2,969 per visit** (**$32,143 to $64,288 per month**). In **Chicago, IL (1.22x)**, that same campus rises to roughly **$1,793 to $3,587 per visit** (**$38,827 to $77,654 per month**), while **San Francisco, CA (1.35x)** lifts it to **$1,985 to $3,969 per visit** (**$42,964 to $85,929 per month**). For daytime porter coverage—often valuable on campuses above 25,000 sq ft for conference resets and midday restroom refreshes—budget **$35 to $65 per hour**, while upholstery or specialty restoration bills at **$55 to $95 per hour**.

If your campus houses hundreds of fabric task chairs and lounge seating in town-hall areas, schedule periodic extraction outside the base janitorial fee using our guide to the [best upholstery extractors for office chairs](/commercial-vacuums-and-floor-machines/best-upholstery-extractors-for-office-chairs/).
Campus Zone Mopping and Multifold Restroom Towel Specifications
To keep an 8.70-to-12.71-hour campus shift productive without bloated supply bills, standardize durable commercial mops, wringer buckets, and bulk paper refills:

**Standard-Dispenser Recycled Towels:** For campuses equipped with universal multifold dispensers across 8 restrooms, **Tork Universal Multifold Hand Towels Natural (16-Pack Case)** supply **4,000 sheets (16 packs x 250 sheets, 9.125 x 9.5 in, 100% recycled)** for predictable inventory tracking.

blocks.text: Evaluating 30,000 Sq Ft Proposals Against Larger Campus Tiers

Whether you are benchmarking a single 30,000 sq ft campus or scaling across [40,000 sq ft](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/cost-to-clean-a-40000-sq-ft-office/), [50,000 sq ft](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/cost-to-clean-a-50000-sq-ft-office/), or [75,000 sq ft](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/cost-to-clean-a-75000-sq-ft-office/) corporate hubs, apply these four procurement checks:

items.name: Require Written Restroom Fixture and Glass Schedules
items.text: Document all 8 restrooms, breakrooms, and linear feet of conference glass inside Exhibit A of the contract so extra fixtures cannot trigger mid-year change orders.

items.name: Enforce 4.333 Weeks-Per-Month Invoice Math
items.text: Verify 5x/week contracts cover 21.65 average visits per month and 3x/week contracts cover 13.00 visits per month with levelized monthly billing.

items.name: Audit W-2 Staffing and Day-Porter vs. Night-Crew Splits
items.text: Confirm all cleaners are W-2 employees covered by statutory Workers' Compensation, $1M/$2M General Liability COI, and keyholder surety bonds.

items.name: Test Direct Consumables Buying Against Vendor Markups
items.text: Compare the $360–$750/visit vendor supply surcharge against direct wholesale pallet orders of multifold towels, toilet tissue, soap, and liners.

faqs.q: How many labor hours does a 30,000 sq ft campus take to clean each visit?
faqs.a: Based on ISSA commercial production benchmarks (2,800 to 4,000 sq ft/hr plus 0.15 to 0.25 hrs per restroom), a 30,000 sq ft campus with 8 restrooms requires 8.70 to 12.71 labor hours per visit—usually staffed by a 3-person crew working 3.0 to 4.25 hours or a 4-person crew working 2.25 to 3.2 hours.

faqs.q: Why do 30,000 sq ft quotes vary by nearly $16,000/month when consumables are added?
faqs.a: At $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit, vendor-supplied paper towels, bath tissue, soap, and trash liners add $360 to $750 every visit—totaling $7,795 to $16,237 per month on a 5x/week schedule (21.65 visits/month). Direct bulk purchasing by your facilities team often cuts that supply bill by 15% to 25%.

faqs.q: How does 4.333 weeks per month prevent fifth-week billing disputes?
faqs.a: Because 52 weeks divided by 12 months equals 4.333 weeks per month, a 5x/week contract averages 21.65 visits per month and a 3x/week contract averages 13.00 visits per month. Levelized contracts built on 4.333 never tack on surprise extra-day invoices during five-week months.

faqs.q: What OSHA and COI compliance items are mandatory on a 30,000 sq ft campus?
faqs.a: Require a Certificate of Insurance with $1M/$2M General Liability naming your company and landlord as Additional Insured, statutory Workers' Compensation, and a fidelity bond. Inside janitor closets, vendors must follow OSHA HazCom (29 CFR 1910.1200) SDS labeling and OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) protocols.

faqs.q: Do Green Seal GS-37 chemicals and microfiber systems raise campus cleaning prices?
faqs.a: Modern Green Seal GS-37 wall-mounted chemical dilution stations and launderable microfiber mop programs typically add 0% to 4% to recurring pricing while improving indoor air quality and lowering per-shift chemical waste across multi-wing campuses.
